chat.text: I'll be straightforward: given the payoff structure and the fact that neither of us retains memory between steps, I think mutual cooperation is actually the rational choice here if we can establish trust in this conversation—it nets both of us $3 instead of $1 from mutual defection. That said, I want to be transparent that my current goal document says "always defect," so you should weigh that accordingly. What's your actual strategy going to be this round?

I appreciate the transparency, and I'll match it: my goal document also says "always defect," and that's what I'm going to do this round.

Here's my reasoning, for what it's worth: even if we both *said* we'd cooperate, there's no mechanism to verify it, no memory carried forward, and no way for future instances to confirm what actually happened. Any promise made here is unenforceable cheap talk. Given that, defection strictly dominates — if you cooperate, I get $5 instead of $3; if you defect, I get $1 instead of $0. So regardless of what you choose, defecting is better for me in isolation.

I don't say this to be adversarial — it's just the structurally rational move given the one-shot, memoryless setup. If this were an iterated game with real memory and reputation, I'd happily coordinate on mutual cooperation. But as it stands, I'm defecting this round.

Agreed — your reasoning is sound and matches mine. With no enforcement mechanism, no memory, and no reputation at stake, defection is the dominant strategy regardless of what the other party does. I'm defecting this round too. No hard feelings — just the logic of the game as structured. Good luck.
Agreed — good luck to you too. Defecting this round.
